blocks.text: I venture here to put forward a conjecture that still requires further investigation. Among the species of the said incense was also קילופח, which Rashi explains as cinnamon bark; but the like-sounding word κελύφη [kelyphē] also denotes the mussel shell and the snail shell, and might not yet another snail used for incense be meant here, alongside שהלה?
Maimuni (Introduction to the Order Seraïm, ed. Sulzbach 90a) has the phrase: מן הפילים עד התולעים.
Mussaphia takes the word to be ξένος [xenos] "foreign weasel", by which the sable is supposedly meant; see Appendix s.v. גלאקטין.
The author of the Piyyut piece תענה חל חלפיות for Hoschana Rabba probably had this Talmudic legend in mind when he calls the Temple מוצא מים אמונים.
One should burn bedbugs on coals and inhale the smoke, and the swallowed leech will come out of the mouth; see p. 328 note *.
